page.title: Run review
page.purpose: Let a reviewer judge a conformance run: what each chapter asserted, what it observed, which strategy produced the observation, and whether the evidence can support a release claim at all.

priorities.statement: Each chapter shows expected versus observed, not just pass or fail.
priorities.notes: A reviewer cannot judge a verdict they cannot see the basis for.

priorities.statement: A run built from non-promotable evidence says so at the top, not in a footnote.
priorities.notes: A green non-promotable run is the most dangerous artifact this scenario can produce, because it looks exactly like a releasable one.

priorities.statement: Every chapter names the strategy that produced it and whether that strategy is semantic or pixel-grade.
priorities.notes: The same chapter carries very different weight depending on whether an accessibility tree or OCR produced it.

priorities.statement: A bounded policy that was exceeded reads as a failure with its bound, never as a longer wait.
priorities.notes: Silently extending a wait converts a real defect into a slow pass.

elements.name: Run verdict
elements.description: The overall disposition for the run, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Conformance chapters
elements.description: The chaptered timeline in execution order.

elements.name: Expected
elements.description: The asserted expectation for one chapter.

elements.name: Chapter strategy
elements.description: The device-control strategy that produced this chapter and its capability tier.

elements.name: Promotability
elements.description: Statement that this run's evidence cannot contribute to a release gate. Present only when the run is non-promotable.

elements.name: Exceeded bound
elements.description: The readiness or settle bound a failing chapter exceeded, with its limit.

elements.name: Journey recording
elements.description: The captured recording, offered alongside the timeline and never as the only way to read the result.

elements.name: Lease interruption
elements.description: The notice shown when a run terminated because its device-control lease was lost or revoked rather than because the application misbehaved.

states.description: A complete passing run on a simulator via ios-simctl, semantic tier, with a decoded recording.
The run record is being fetched; no chapters are asserted yet.
No runs exist for this target yet. Explains how to start one rather than showing an empty timeline.
Native shell chapters ran; web-content chapters are unavailable because BAS could not attach to the WKWebView. The run reports partial honestly rather than passing.
The run predates the current generated artifact, so its verdict may not describe what would ship today.
The run record could not be loaded. Reported as a failure rather than as an empty or failed run.
A run in progress; completed chapters are readable and pending ones are explicitly pending, not blank.
One chapter failed on an assertion. The failing expectation and observation are both visible.
Every chapter passed, but the run was driven by ios-mirror. The run is green and explicitly cannot contribute to a release gate.
The run ended early because its device-control lease was revoked mid-run. Chapters completed before the interruption are retained; the run is incomplete rather than failed.

claims.statement: Every asserted chapter displays both its expected value and its observed value.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-006. A verdict without its basis cannot be reviewed, only trusted.

claims.statement: A run whose evidence cannot gate a release presents an explicit promotability notice.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-010. A green non-promotable run looks exactly like a releasable one; only an explicit statement separates them.

claims.statement: A semantically driven passing run carries no promotability notice.
claims.rationale: The notice must mean something. Showing it on every run would train reviewers to ignore it.

claims.statement: The promotability notice is visible without scrolling.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-010. A footnote that a run cannot gate a release is functionally the same as not saying it.

claims.statement: Every chapter names its executing strategy and capability tier.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. A semantic assertion and an OCR match are different kinds of evidence and must never be presented identically.

claims.statement: A chapter whose readiness or settle bound was exceeded displays the bound it exceeded alongside a failed verdict.
claims.rationale: Bounded policies exist so slowness is a signal. Presenting an exceeded bound as anything else destroys that signal.

claims.statement: The run verdict and chapter timeline are present independently of the recording.
claims.rationale: Video is evidence, not interface. The verdict must be legible in text.

claims.statement: A run with unavailable chapters renders distinguishably from a fully passing run.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-010. Unavailable is terminal for the cell and cannot be promoted.

claims.statement: Two runs where every chapter passed still render distinguishably when one cannot gate a release.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-010. This is the exact pair a reviewer is most likely to confuse, because both are green.

claims.statement: A run terminated by a lost device-control lease renders distinguishably from a run in which a chapter assertion failed.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. One is an infrastructure interruption and the other is evidence about the application. Rendering them alike sends a reviewer to debug an application that was behaving correctly.

claims.statement: A lease-interrupted run presents an explicit interruption notice naming the lost lease.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. An early-terminated run with no stated cause is indistinguishable from a crash.

claims.statement: A lease-interrupted run carries a promotability notice, because an incomplete chapter set cannot support a release claim.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. Partial evidence that reads as neutral is the mechanism by which an unproven build reaches a release gate.
